source.text: בהנחל עליון גוים בהפרידו בני אדם יצב גבלת עמים למספר בני אלוהים׃
source.note: Provisional editorial composite: unpointed WLC base with final בני ישראל replaced by published 4Q37 בני אלוהים. Unchanged units retain base interpretation and spelling, including בהנחל. The complete verse does not survive in 4Q37; no original vowel points or autograph recovered. Source priority remains provisional.

apparatus.note: Direct contrary Hebrew reading; coherent retrospective Israel-number interpretation retained.
Selected final phrase outside brackets in the published transcription. One fragmentary Hebrew excerpt, not a complete verse; no new blind image collation.
Opening yod outside brackets, following context supplied. This composite retains base בהנחל without claiming earlier defective spelling.
Angels of God: divine-referent versional support, not a unique Hebrew retroversion.
Normalized surviving sons prefix with omega doubtful in the edition; complement lost. God/Israel cannot be decided by this fragment.
Correcting-hand sons of Israel report; no new correction-image or modern adjacent-apparatus consultation.
Exact Deuteronomy wording not directly attested in the consulted sample. The separately reported 1QHa allusion is not independently collated here.

translation.text: When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when he separated humankind[b], he fixed the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of God[a].

footnotes.text: POB provisionally follows the published 4Q37 reading, “sons of God”; the Masoretic Text and Samaritan Pentateuch read “sons of Israel.” The main Greek Septuagint reading is “angels of God.” The exact earliest Hebrew remains debated; “sons of El” is a conjectural Deuteronomy reading. The rest of this verse retains the Masoretic base; it is not a complete surviving 4Q37 text.
Hebrew: “sons of humankind,” paralleling “sons of God” later in the verse. The expression refers to human beings, not only males.

lexical_decisions.rationale: The Hiphil infinitive construct of נחל with prefixed ב marks a temporal clause, and in context refers to assigning inheritances among nations. 'Gave the nations their inheritance' is idiomatic English that preserves the distributive sense better than a wooden 'caused to inherit.'
A divine title here. English convention normally includes the article in this construction, and 'the Most High' preserves the title's force without paraphrase.

In Deuteronomy this refers to the various peoples/nations of the world, not specifically 'Gentiles' in a later Jewish-Christian contrast. The article is supplied for natural English reference to the class as a whole.
Another temporal infinitive construct with 3ms suffix referring back to the Most High. 'Separated' fits the plain sense of פרד here and pairs well with the following object.

The phrase denotes human beings. Humankind makes that collective reference clear in modern English; the note retains the repeated sons construction linking this phrase to בני אלוהים. Current doctrine permits man or humankind by context and does not impose the historical masculine-form mandate. No new lexicon consultation is claimed.

Under the retained base vocalization, the Hiphil imperfect describes setting the boundaries. The vendored OSHB control assigns lemma 5324 (נצב), word ID 05kX5, morphology HVhi3ms. Fixed renders the setting firmly in the narrated past; this corrects the former root attribution, not the Hebrew text. The edition annotation is not independent ancient evidence.
'Boundaries' fits territorial delimitation, and 'peoples' avoids repeating 'nations' too closely while still matching עמים as ethnic/political groups.

alternatives: in proportion to the number of
lexical_decisions.rationale: This prepositional phrase indicates correspondence or measure. 'According to the number of' is the most idiomatic and sufficiently formal rendering.

Render the selected attested phrase without erasing its sons imagery. Divine beings clarifies the referent but is more interpretive. Israel and El are separate source alternatives disclosed in the apparatus and note, not lexical glosses of the selected phrase. This does not determine biological parentage or whether Most High and Yahweh designate distinct beings.

theological_decisions.issue: Textual variant in the final clause
theological_decisions.rationale: The provisional full-source decision selects attested בני אלוהים with moderate referent confidence. The text and reader note distinguish MT/SP Israel, Greek angels and conjectural El. The selection does not establish the earliest exact form, an explicit divine headcount, or a particular relationship between Most High and Yahweh. The old WLC label must not be retained for this composite.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: DOCTRINE.md: original-language primacy, preserve theological tension, and source distinctions.

theological_decisions.rationale: Modern collective wording preserves the human referent, with the parallel sons idiom disclosed in the note. Grammatical masculinity does not require restricting the referent to males or invoking a superseded policy.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: DOCTRINE.md: readable modern English; אדם man / humankind by context.

value.text: בְּ/הַנְחֵ֤ל עֶלְיוֹן֙ גּוֹיִ֔ם בְּ/הַפְרִיד֖/וֹ בְּנֵ֣י אָדָ֑ם יַצֵּב֙ גְּבֻלֹ֣ת עַמִּ֔ים לְ/מִסְפַּ֖ר בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of man[b], he fixed the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel[a].

footnotes.text: 4QDeutj (4Q37) reads “sons of God”; the Septuagint reads “angels of God.” The Samaritan Pentateuch agrees with the Masoretic “sons of Israel.” The divine-being reading is likely earlier, although its precise Hebrew form and interpretation remain debated.
'The sons of man' is a Hebrew expression for human beings or humankind.

value.rationale: The Hiphil infinitive construct of נחל with prefixed ב marks a temporal clause, and in context refers to assigning inheritances among nations. 'Gave the nations their inheritance' is idiomatic English that preserves the distributive sense better than a wooden 'caused to inherit.'

In Deuteronomy this refers to the various peoples/nations of the world, not specifically 'Gentiles' in a later Jewish-Christian contrast. The article is supplied for natural English reference to the class as a whole.

Per the project's gender-accurate policy, the masculine form is retained where the Hebrew is explicitly masculine and representative. 'Sons of man' is a fairly literal rendering of בני אדם and preserves the poetic register. A more inclusive sense is possible, but the source expression is not flattened in the main text.
The Hiphil of יצב conveys setting firmly or establishing. 'Fixed' communicates decisive placement of boundaries in natural English.
'Boundaries' fits territorial delimitation, and 'peoples' avoids repeating 'nations' too closely while still matching עמים as ethnic/political groups.

value.rationale: This prepositional phrase indicates correspondence or measure. 'According to the number of' is the most idiomatic and sufficiently formal rendering.

The Masoretic Text reads 'sons of Israel,' which is rendered transparently while this verse remains sourced to WLC. Direct Hebrew manuscript 4Q37 instead reads 'sons of God,' and the restoration assessment currently prefers that divine referent; a main-text change must be coordinated with an explicit critical-source promotion rather than made silently in English. 'Children of Israel' is traditional but less formally precise; 'Israelites' is interpretive rather than lexical.

value.issue: Textual variant in the final clause
value.rationale: The WLC source field reads בני ישראל ('sons of Israel'), so the current English remains synchronized to that recorded source. Direct Hebrew manuscript 4Q37 reads בני אלוהים ('sons of God'), while the Septuagint has 'angels of God.' The restoration assessment currently prefers the divine referent, but canonical promotion requires the selected critical source and English to change together. The materially different reading is therefore stated precisely in the footnote rather than silently substituted.
value.doctrine_reference: Translation philosophy §1 (original-language primacy over translation tradition) and §3 (preserve theological tension rather than resolve it).

value.rationale: The Hebrew is grammatically masculine and representative. In keeping with the project's gender-accurate policy, the main text preserves the masculine form rather than replacing it with a gender-neutral paraphrase, while acknowledging the broader human reference in a footnote.
